extracted.intended_audience: general public — parents, teachers, dressmakers, health-seekers (Victorian-era readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for designing, choosing, and wearing clothing so as to promote bodily health — addressing mechanical fit, seasonal amount, ventilation, materials, dyes, cleanliness, and social practices. Emphasizes avoiding constriction and carrying garments from the waist, and adapting fashion to hygienic principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress in relation to its mechanical adaptation to the body
rubrics_metrics.description: Dress must be mechanically adapted to the body so as to permit freedom of motion and not impede physiological function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equable general pressure that gives support and yields with growth may be acceptable, but any plan that leads to irregular tightening or compression (tight corsets, waist-belts, tight straps) is to be abandoned. Compression can suppress breathing, the heart-beat, and digestion; displace organs; prevent full growth of organs during development; and have lifelong harmful consequences. Exceptional cases (support in advanced life) require special, elastic adaptation that permits freedom of motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pressure used to produce an artificial shape
rubrics_metrics.description: The deliberate use of tight pressure to mould the body into an unnatural outline for fashion is harmful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fashionable compression (corsets, tight waist-belts) produces artificial outlines at the expense of respiratory, circulatory, and digestive function and retards organ growth. Such practices are condemned as destructive of physical and mental capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four particularly injurious pressure-locations to avoid: waist, foot, leg, neck
rubrics_metrics.description: Pressure at the waist, on the feet, round the leg (garters), and round the neck (tight collars/cravats) are the most harmful varieties of constriction in dress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author places them in order of importance (waist greatest). Waist compression (corsets/belts) impairs lungs/heart/digestion and may cause displacement; tight footwear deforms feet; garters worn low impede venous return and contribute to varicose veins; tight collars/cravats can obstruct venous return from the brain, especially in plethoric individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belts and strapped support are harmful, not helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: Using belts or straps to 'support' clothing or to 'hold in the breath' is a fashion with no physiologic basis and is injurious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Belts impede respiration, compress abdominal and back muscles, impede motion, promote hernia by forcing abdominal contents downward under exertion, and produce lasting injury. Men and boys who habitually wear belts suffer harm similar in kind to corset wearers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footwear should approximate the natural foot — avoid tight, pointed shoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Boots and shoes should approach the natural form of the foot; pointed or tight footwear deforms and weakens the foot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointed/toe-compressing shoes force the great toe out of line, compress other toes, create a wedge-like foot with lost expanse, weakened arch, increased corns and bunions, poorer nutrition and circulation, and an altered, awkward gait. Tight boots in general are to be discarded in favour of shapes close to the natural foot; prefer designs that allow the arch free play and elastic action (e.g., Mr. Dowie's elastic arch band).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid raised heels that derange the foot's arch
rubrics_metrics.description: Raised heels (above the level of the palm of the foot) are anatomically and physiologically mistaken and injurious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raising the heel deranges the arch, prevents the foot's elastic wave-like motion, causes concussion up the spinal column at each step, and limits the foot's ability to seize the earth, leading to inefficient and exhausting muscular compensation. Removal or reduction of the raised heel is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garters and bands should not constrict veins; avoid wearing them below the knee
rubrics_metrics.description: Ligatures such as garters produce a ring of depression and can seriously impede venous return from the foot and leg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Garters are unhealthy in any position but are particularly bad when worn below the knee because they compress veins without tendon support, and contribute to varicose veins and impede recovery from venous disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing must admit atmospheric air to the skin
rubrics_metrics.description: Dress should permit the admission of atmospheric air through it or beneath it to the surface of the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate ventilation of the skin is an important hygienic consideration (heading promised discussion). Clothing should balance protection from weather with allowing airflow to the body surface to preserve health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress amount should be appropriate to season (adjust to English climate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of clothing worn should be varied according to seasonal changes and the local climate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Garments should be chosen and adjusted to provide suitable warmth and protection in different seasons; rapid changeability and ease of altering dress are valuable for coping with vicissitudes of weather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider color of materials in relation to health
rubrics_metrics.description: The colour of the material composing dress is a factor to be considered in relation to health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour choice is listed as a distinct hygienic topic; the implication is that colour affects thermal properties, visibility, and perhaps psychological/behavioral factors, and should be considered when selecting materials (further specifics are signaled but not elaborated in this excerpt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid harmful dyes and coloring substances contacting the skin
rubrics_metrics.description: The action of colouring substances introduced into fabrics that come into contact with the surface of the body must be considered for health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials dyed with injurious colouring substances can have deleterious effects when in contact with the skin; selection of safe fabrics and dyes is a hygiene concern (heading noted; specific chemical guidance not provided here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleanliness in dress
rubrics_metrics.description: Cleanliness of clothing is a serious hygienic requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clean garments are essential for health; the author enumerates 'Cleanliness in dress' as a primary topic and treats it as a fundamental standard of hygienic attire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support clothing from the shoulders rather than the waist
rubrics_metrics.description: Clothing (especially heavy or layered female dress) should be borne by the shoulders, not tied and supported from the waist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carrying garments from the waist (girdles, tied layers) imposes weight and pressure akin to corsetry, drags on the body, impedes movement, and is unjustifiable. The shoulders are the anatomically appropriate load-bearing area; adopting shoulder support for women's dress would provide health and freedom of movement while preserving graceful outer gowns as desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing should cover the body equally and allow easy change
rubrics_metrics.description: Healthy dress provides even coverage, leaves limbs free, is easy to put on and off, and allows ready change with weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Men's modern dress is commended for equal coverage and for being borne by the shoulders, permitting breathing, circulation, and easy alteration; women should adopt these practical advantages except for maintaining a graceful outer robe. Equal, balanced clothing is a hygienic ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat cultural transmission of deforming dress practices through education
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach children (especially girls) not to adopt deforming dress practices, because the proclivity to such practices is culturally/hereditarily transmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that while the physical deformity may not be genetically transmitted, the tendency and desire to perform deforming acts are inherited socially. Educators and parents must fight inbred proclivities by reforming young people's dress habits; abandoning tight lacing and tight footwear now will take generations to eliminate entrenched habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good fashion and good health ought to align
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing incompatible between good fashion and good health; hygienic improvements should be combined with tasteful fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author insists that good fashion can and should be made hygienic, and that national taste should adopt hygienic dressing as part of fashionable design. Fashion leaders should not set trends that set 'Nature at defiance.'
